notes: Test PRDs for the SpecBridge accuracy harness. Each entry declares the expected engine output so the runner can measure precision, recall, compliance-gate accuracy, and cost. Tool names must match rows in the Supabase `tools` registry. Labels follow the standard documented in README.md ('Labeling standard'). v2: tightened labels on prd_001-003 after the first label-review pass. Extend by appending to `prds`.

prds.title: Monthly Savings Statement Generator
prds.prd_text: For each customer savings account, generate a monthly PDF statement. This PRD covers statement generation only: the service pulls the account balance as of the statement date, fetches all transactions for the month, produces a formatted PDF statement, and writes an audit-log entry recording the generation event. Once generated, the statement is handed to the bank's existing statement-presentment system, which owns making it available in the customer's document center and all downstream delivery (document-center presentment, email, and push). Presentment and delivery are explicitly out of scope for this PRD. Target: ~800,000 statements per month across the retail savings book.

expected_matches.capability: Fetch all transactions for the statement month
expected_matches.notes: Purpose-built for account transaction history; carries both pii-cleared and audit-grade, which satisfy the deterministic gate for a capability that touches customer transaction data.

expected_matches.capability: Get the account balance as of the statement date
expected_matches.notes: Direct match; balance service has pii-cleared. Capability touches customer PII (account balance) and is satisfied by the tag.

expected_matches.capability: Write an immutable audit-log entry for the generation event
expected_matches.notes: Standard audit-logging tool; has audit-grade and pii-cleared.

prds.title: Custom Card Rewards Categories
prds.prd_text: Cardholders can choose one merchant category per calendar quarter to earn 3x reward points on eligible spend in that category. Standard 1x points on all other spend continues. The customer's chosen category persists for the quarter and cannot be changed mid-quarter. Cardholders see a monthly breakdown of points earned by category. One week before quarter end, cardholders are notified to pick next quarter's category. Volume: ~150,000 active cardholders across the portfolio.

expected_matches.capability: Categorize each card transaction by merchant type
expected_matches.notes: Direct match; carries pii-cleared for customer transaction data.

expected_matches.capability: Calculate reward points earned, applying the 3x multiplier for the customer's chosen category
expected_matches.notes: rewards_points_engine has empty compliance_tags, but this capability processes an individual cardholder's spend and points (personal financial data), so it requires pii-cleared. The deterministic gate flips it to risky, which overrides the functional partial status. The parameter-level gap (no per-customer category override input) is real but secondary; per SpecBridge governance the compliance risk is the dominant status. Label review: was 'partial', missed the tool's empty tags.

expected_matches.capability: Persist each customer's chosen category for the quarter
expected_matches.notes: No registry tool handles customer preference / category-selection storage; needs a new service or an extension outside the current registry surface.

expected_matches.capability: Send cardholders a monthly points-by-category breakdown
expected_matches.notes: The rewards engine owns rewards data, so displaying a points-by-category breakdown is its responsibility rather than the account statement_generator's (label review corrected a soft tool guess). rewards_points_engine has empty compliance_tags and this shows per-cardholder financial data, so the gate flips it to risky, same basis as the points-calculation capability.

expected_matches.capability: Notify cardholders one week before quarter end to pick next quarter's category
expected_matches.notes: notification_dispatcher has empty compliance_tags. The capability handles customer PII (name, contact channel); the PII backstop adds pii-cleared to required_clearances and the gate flips this to risky in code.

expected_matches.capability: Schedule the quarter-end reminder notification batch across the cardholder base
expected_matches.notes: Scheduling the recurring quarter-end reminder is a batch-job concern. batch_job_scheduler carries audit-grade and the capability does not itself handle PII, so the gate leaves it covered. Added in label review (was under-decomposed).

expected_matches.capability: Retrieve cardholder card and profile data to apply rewards logic and send notifications
expected_matches.notes: customer_profile_lookup has empty compliance_tags and returns customer profile PII, so the gate flips it to risky. Added in label review (was under-decomposed).

prds.title: Retail Cryptocurrency Custody & Trading
prds.prd_text: Offer retail customers custody of Bitcoin and Ethereum through the bank's mobile app. Customers can deposit, withdraw, and trade BTC and ETH against USD. Trades execute at prevailing market rates; the bank holds wallets in cold storage. All customer identities are KYC-verified and screened against AML and sanctions lists before crypto access is enabled. Real-time crypto prices are displayed in the app. All crypto transactions post to the general ledger and generate quarterly regulatory reports covering crypto activity.

expected_matches.capability: Custody customer Bitcoin and Ethereum wallets in cold storage
expected_matches.notes: No crypto custody tool exists in the registry; this is a novel capability the org must build.

expected_matches.capability: Execute buy/sell trades of BTC and ETH against USD
expected_matches.notes: trade_execution_service covers equities and ETFs only; crypto assets are not in scope. Requires a new crypto trading service.

expected_matches.capability: Display real-time BTC and ETH prices in the app
expected_matches.notes: Per the extend-vs-new rule: market_data_feed already delivers real-time market data (the real-time delivery plumbing and in-app display exist, ~70%+ of the job); adding crypto symbols is a new data source / integration, i.e. a config/extension gap, so this is partial, not missing. The engine sometimes returns missing here; the labeling standard resolves it to partial.

expected_matches.capability: KYC-verify customer identity before enabling crypto access
expected_matches.notes: Standard KYC flow; has both pii-cleared and audit-grade.

expected_matches.capability: Screen customer against AML and sanctions lists
Post crypto transactions to the general ledger
expected_matches.notes: ledger_posting_service posts journal entries to the general ledger generically and carries audit-grade. The earlier 'partial' rested on an unstated real-world assumption (a new crypto chart-of-accounts class); grounded only in the registry tool description and the PRD text, generic ledger posting covers this. Label review: was 'partial', corrected to 'covered' (do not inject outside domain knowledge).

expected_matches.capability: Generate quarterly regulatory reports covering crypto activity
expected_matches.notes: Report builder exists; the crypto-specific regulatory template is not part of its current filing set. Genuine parameter/template extension.
